a b s t r a c t 
An eﬃcient method for the regioselective preparation of 1,3-dimethylenecyclobutanes based on Ru- 
catalyzed dimerization of readily available CF 3 -containing functionalized allenes including α-amino acid 
derivatives have been developed. The reactions smoothly proceed in toluene at 100 °C in the presence of 
catalytic amounts (5 mol%) of naphthalene-containing ruthenium system [Cp ∗Ru(C 10 H 8 )]PF 6 /[Et 3 NBn]Cl to 
afford exclusively tail-to-tail coupling products in good to excellent yields.

1. Introduction 
Cyclobutanes are important structural motifs of many biologi- 
cally active molecules including natural products [1] and are also 
valuable intermediates for a range of useful chemical transforma- 
tions [2] . One of the straightforward and atom-economic access to 
cyclobutane ring construction is based on [2 + 2] cycloaddition of 
allenes [3] . Despite the thermal version of this transformation is 
well studied process [4] , the control of regioselectivity (head-to- 
tail, tail-to-tail, head-to-head) [5] is often hard to achieve. On the 
other hand, less investigated dimerization of allenes catalyzed by 
transition metals (Ni [6] , Pd [7] , Au [8] , Rh [9] , Ru [10] ) has been 
shown to be an eﬃcient alternative strategy to provide the cy- 
clobutane ring systems in regioselective manner. However, these 
catalytic methods mainly lead to 1,2-methylencyclobutanes with 
the only exception for Ru(II)-catalysis. Thus, Dixneuf and coworkers 
successfully realized tail-to-tail cycloaddition of allenyl boronate 
under catalysis with Cp ∗Ru(cod)Cl to establish the ﬁrst direct path- 
way to regioselective formation of 1,3-methylencyclobutanes [10] . 
The interest to latter compounds deals with their great potential 
to be utilized as the key precursors for the generation of the cor-

responding cyclobutane-2,4-diradicals with triplet ground state to 
apply in material science as paramagnetic building blocks [11] . 
On the other hand, organoﬂuorine compounds ﬁnd nowadays 
more and more important applications in modern life and material 
sciences [12] . This fact stimulate the researchers to develop new 
eﬃcient methodologies for the introduction of ﬂuorine and ﬂuori- 
nated groups into different organic molecules. 
In a recent study, we have developed an eﬃcient one-step ac- 
cess to functionalized allenes 2 via [ 2 , 3 ]-sigmatropic rearrange- 
ment of propargyl-containing nitrogen ylides generated in situ 
from CF 3 -containing diazo compounds 1 ( Scheme 1 A) [13] . The 
synthetic potential of 2 has been demonstrated by their inter- 
and intramolecular transformations under catalysis with transition 
metals [14] , e.g. such as Cu-catalyzed hydroamination [14a] or Co- 
catalyzed Pauson-Khand reaction [13] to afford the corresponding 
α-amino acid derivatives ( Scheme 1 B). Now we wish to report 
on a convenient pathway to new triﬂuoromethyl-containing 1,3- 
dimetylencyclobutanes via dimerization of functionalized allenes 
under Ru-catalysis ( Scheme 1 C). 
2. Results and discussion 
Our continuous interest in the development of eﬃcient meth- 
ods for the preparation of diverse CF 3 -containing compounds 
based on metal-catalyzed transformations of unsaturated pre- 
cursors including alkynyl- and alkenyl α-amino acid derivatives

[15] prompted us to explore the reactivity of functionally substi- 
tuted allenes in dimerization process catalyzed by Ru-complexes. 
In our initial attempt, being inspired by Dixneuf’s ﬁnding [10] , 
we examined the catalytic activity of Cp ∗Ru(cod)Cl in intramolec- 
ular [2 + 2] cyclization of allene 2a chosen as model substrate. 
Thus, we found that the reaction takes place when boiling in 
dichloroethane (DCE) in the presence of 3 mol% of catalyst lead- 
ing to formation of the desired cyclobutane 3a in 78% yield for 2 
hours ( Table 1 , entry 1). The replacing the solvent with toluene, 
increasing the temperature (up to100 °C) and catalyst loading up 
to 5 mol% led to 98% yield of 3a (entry 3). Then we tested the 
activity of naphthalene complex [Cp ∗Ru(C 10 H 8 )]PF 6 , which gener- 
ates the same active species [Cp ∗RuCl] in the presence of chloride 
ion [16] . This catalyst is a more convenient one to work with than 
[Cp ∗Ru(cod)Cl], because it is air-stable and easily accessible by us- 
ing a one-step procedure from RuCl 3 •3H 2 O [17] . After variation 
of solvent, catalyst loading and reaction temperature the quanti- 
tative yield of 3a has been achieved when the reaction was per- 
formed with 5 mol% of naphthalene-containing catalytic system 
[Cp ∗Ru(C 10 H 8 )]PF 6 /[Et 3 NBn]Cl in toluene at 100 °C for 2 hours (en- 
try 6). When the reaction was carried out in the absence of any 
catalyst, no product was observed (entry 7). Monitoring of the re- 
action in all cases was accomplished using 19 F NMR spectroscopy 
and TLC analysis. 
As result, ruthenium catalytic system [Cp ∗Ru(C 10 H 8 )]PF 6 / 
[Et 3 NBn]Cl was chosen as preferential catalyst for dimerization 
process. With the optimized conditions in hand, we examined the 
reactivity of three more allenes bearing N(Me)Bn ( 2b ), ethyl car- 
boxylate ( 2c ) and phosphonate ( 2d ) groups, which were prepared 
by the same way using previously described protocol ( Scheme 1 A). 
In all cases the corresponding 1,3methylenecyclobutanes 3b-d were 
obtained in moderate to good yields ( Scheme 2 ). 
1,3-Methylenecyclobutanes 3a - d were initially isolated as cis- 
, trans -isomer mixtures in a ratio indicated on Scheme 2 (deter- 
mined by 1 Н and 19 F NMR spectroscopy). The compounds 3a,b and 
3d bearing asymmetric center additionally formed diastereomers 
in equal amounts approximately, which can be easily separated by 
column chromatography on silica gel. In the case of 3b and 3d we 
were successful to separate in addition cis- and trans -isomers in 
the individual forms (see Supporting Info). The characterization of 
the compounds obtained was performed using standard physico- 
chemical methods and elemental analysis. The assignment of sig- 
nals of cis- and trans -isomers in the mixtures was achieved by 2D 
NOESY NMR experiments. While for both isomers dipolar cross- 
peaks appears between oleﬁne and cyclobutane protons, they are 
signiﬁcantly more intense in the case of the trans -isomer, reﬂecting 
larger number of interacting nuclei ( Fig. 1 ). 
In addition, the structures of individual stereoisomers of 3a-c 
were determined by X-ray diffraction ( Fig. 2 ). 
In the case of allenynes 2e [13] , 2f [14c] and 2g [14c], likely 
due to the presence of an additional triple bond capable to coor- 
dinate with catalytic species, the reaction leads to the complicated 
mixture of the products that were impossible to identify. There- 
fore, we decided to block triple bond by Cu(I)-catalyzed “click” re-

3. Conclusion 
We have developed a direct catalytic access to 1,3- 
dimethylenecyclobutanes based on dimerization of readily 
available CF 3 -substituted functional allenes under Ru-catalysis. 
The reactions smoothly proceed in toluene at 100 °C in the 
presence of 5 mol% naphthalene-containing ruthenium catalytic 
system [Cp ∗Ru(C 10 H 8 )]PF 6 /[Et 3 NBn]Cl exclusively affording tail-to- 
tail allene dimerization products in good to excellent yields. The 
corresponding 1,3-dimethylenecyclobutane derivatives are formed 
as mixtures of cis,trans -isomers that can be separated by column 
chromatography. Functionalized allenynes can be also applied for 
Ru-catalyzed dimerization after blocking of triple bond by means 
of triazole formation via Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne ligation.

reference).

4.4. General procedure for the synthesis of triazole-containing allenes 
To a solution of the corresponding acetylene-containing allene 
(0.14 g, 0.54 mmol) in t BuOH/H 2 O (1:1 ratio) (5 mL) was added the 
benzyl azide or pivaloyl methyl azide (0.08g, 0.54 mmol), sodium 
ascorbate (21.5 mg, 0.1 mmol) and 0.5 M copper sulfate pentahy- 
drate (0.03 mmol) sequentially. The reaction mixture was stirred 
at room temperature for 7 h. Upon the completion of the reaction 
(monitored) by TLC the mixed solvent was removed under reduced

and the solvent removed under reduced pressure to afford crude 
triazole. Column chromatography (eluent petroleum ether/ethyl ac- 
etate) provided the pure target products.
